All three new files use native qwen2 metadata and NFC-normalized inputs. They were checked on B200 with the same pinned runtime and inputs as the preceding batch; the BF16 reference results are reused from that batch.

Every 27B quant gives something up. These give up less. We measured the leading public GGUFs against the full BF16 model on one protocol. At every size we ship, ours is the closest to Qwen’s next-token distribution.

This is huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-abliterated (Gyro-S, Gyro-M) and its v2 (Gyro-L), encoded the same way as our Gyro files. Abliteration is huihui-ai's work: it removes the refusal direction from the model's weights. We only quantized it.

About half of each file is the n-gram (PLE) table, which stays on disk and is read row by row. It is the base model's table, the same for every Qwen3.8-Flash-Next quant, so it does not need to come with every file.

Hy4-preview-Q4_K_M.gguf — a conventional Q4_K_M. Most tensors are Q4_K; ffn_down_exps gets Q6_K on 37 layers via llama.cpp's own logic. Use this unless you are memory-constrained.
Clean answers, structured reasoning, agent instincts — and the transcript artifacts that leaked into v1's replies are gone.

Parable-Granite-4.1-8B is an ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b fine-tune trained on real multi-step agent sessions: planning, tool use, and reasoning captured from actual Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.5 agent work, not synthetic Q&A. It is the largest release in the Parable series.
A 4B local coding model with agent instincts. Planning, tool habits and terminal reasoning distilled from real Claude Fable 5 agent sessions, not synthetic Q&A. Runs on ~2.5 GB of RAM.
Every answer opens with a ... reasoning block — native to Qwen3, reinforced by this fine-tune. llama.cpp's --jinja chat mode separates it automatically; strip it before showing replies to end users.
This quants are specific for the DS4 inference engine. They may work with other inference engines or not (they should, but not the MTP model which requires a specific loader).

The n-grams are copied byte-for-byte from Qwen's original checkpoint at de4b8e4d43b917e7706784d8bb445c9af86a3540, including its padding rows. The packer checks the original hash constants and verifies every copied payload.

KLD and top-1 are against the original, unmodified BF16 model, so they hold the edit and the quantization together. Most of it is the edit: on BF16 weights the edit alone is 0.204 (82.5% same top-1), and our plain AD-Q8_0 of the original is 0.063.
Built by the team behind Atomic Chat , the app that runs open-weight models locally and offline.

Ling 3.0 flash is a 124B MoE with 5.1B active parameters; its GGUF chat template includes thinking mode and tool calling. Our AD layouts have 31–41% lower mean KL than stock llama.cpp presets at comparable sizes. The raw measurements and controls are public.
With --jinja the model's own chat template starts every answer in thinking mode; turn it off per request with "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}.

51B of the model's 177B parameters are not weights in the usual sense. They are an n-gram lookup table. The model hashes the last three tokens, and that hash points at 16 rows of 160 values each. Roughly 2.7 KB per token, read once per forward pass, out of a 39 GB table.
